Surah As-Sajdah [Meccan, and its verses are thirty]

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it.

﴿The revelation of the Book﴾: al-Qur'an is the mubtada' (subject of the nominal sentence; the topic). ﴿There is no doubt﴾: shakk (doubt) ﴿in it﴾ is the first khabar (predicate). ﴿From the Lord of the worlds﴾ is the second khabar.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 3:

﴿Am﴾ (rather): ﴿do they say, "He has invented it"﴾? Muhammad (ﷺ)? No. ﴿Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, that you may warn﴾ by it ﴿a people to whom no warner has come before you [ma] (negative) [and] ﴿so that they may be guided﴾ by your warning.

﴿Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾, the first of them Sunday and the last of them Friday. ﴿Then He established Himself over the Throne﴾. Linguistically, it (al-'arsh) is the couch of kingship, [and] an *istiwa'* (establishment, settling) befitting Him. ﴿You have not﴾, O disbelievers of Mecca, ﴿besides Him﴾, i.e., other than Him, ﴿any protector﴾, the noun *ma* with *min* added as an extra particle, i.e., any helper. ﴿Nor any intercessor﴾ who would ward off His punishment from you. ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ This, so that you would believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 5:

﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth﴾, (for the duration of the world). ﴿Then it ascends to Him﴾, (the affair and its arrangement return) ﴿in a Day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count﴾ in the world. In Surat Sa'ala (al-Ma'arij), it is fifty thousand years, and this is the Day of Resurrection, because of the severity of its terrors for the disbeliever. As for the believer, it will be lighter for him than an obligatory prayer that he performs in the world, as has come in the hadith.

That (is) the Creator who governs, ﴿the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, i.e., what is absent from the creation and what is present; ﴿the Mighty﴾, the Invincible in His dominion, ﴿the Merciful﴾ toward the people of His obedience.

The one who made excellent everything He created: ﴿Who made everything He created good﴾. With a fatha on the lam, "khalaqahu" is a past-tense verb serving as a descriptive qualifier (ṣifah). With a sukun on it, it is a badal ishtimal (inclusive apposition, a substitute noun that encompasses the thing it replaces). ﴿And He began the creation of man﴾, meaning Adam.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 32, verse 8:

﴿Then He made his offspring﴾ (nasl) his descendants (dhurriyyah) ﴿from an extract﴾ (sulalah) a drop (ʿalaqah) ﴿of a despised fluid﴾ (ma' maheen), weak, which is the sperm-drop (nutfah).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti), on Surah 32, verse 9:

﴿Then He proportioned him﴾, i.e., the creation of Adam; ﴿and breathed into him of His spirit﴾, i.e., He made him living and sentient after he had been inanimate matter; ﴿and made for you﴾, i.e., for his offspring, ﴿hearing﴾, in the sense of hearing faculties, ﴿and sight, and hearts﴾, i.e., minds/hearts; ﴿little are the thanks you give﴾. The ﴿mā﴾ here is extra (zā'idah), emphasizing the smallness (of the thanks).

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 32, verse 10:**

﴿And they say﴾, that is, those who deny the Resurrection (al-ba'th), ﴿"When we have strayed (ḍalalnā) into the earth?"﴾ meaning, when we have become lost and hidden within it, by becoming dust mixed with its dust. ﴿"Shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ This is a question of denial (istifhām inkār). The two hamzahs are pronounced fully (taḥqīq), the second may be softened (tasḥīl), and an alif may be inserted between them, in both ways, in both places. ﴿Nay, but they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾, that is, about the Resurrection.

*Note on the grammar: the two hamzahs in the words أإذا (ʾa-idhā, "when, is it?") and أإنّا (ʾa-innā, "is it that we?") may each be read in two ways: the first is always pronounced fully, while the second is either pronounced fully (taḥqīq, "making it clear") or softened (tasḥīl, "easing it"). In either case an alif may be inserted between them, so both forms are permitted at both places.*

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 11:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿The Angel of Death who has been entrusted with you will take your souls﴾, i.e., he will seize your spirits, ﴿then to your Lord you will be returned﴾ alive, so that He may recompense you for your deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 12:

﴿If only you could see when the criminals﴾ (i.e., the disbelievers) ﴿hang their heads before their Lord﴾ (i.e., lowering them in shame), ﴿saying: "Our Lord, we have seen﴾ what we denied of the resurrection ﴿and we have heard﴾ from You the confirmation of the messengers in what we denied them, ﴿so send us back﴾ to the world ﴿that we may do righteousness﴾ in it, ﴿for we are now certain.﴾" But it will not benefit them, and they will not be returned. The answer to "if only" (law) is: you would see a dreadful matter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 13:

﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾ so that it would be guided to faith and obedience by its own choice. ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect﴾ and it is: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together."﴾ The jinn and mankind, all of them. And the keepers (al-khazanah) of Hell will say to them when they enter it:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 14:

﴿So taste⟩ the punishment ﴿for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day⟩, i.e., by your abandoning belief in it. ﴿Indeed, We have forgotten you⟩, i.e., We have left you in the punishment. ﴿And taste the abiding punishment⟩, the everlasting one, ﴿for what you used to do⟩ of disbelief and denial.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 15:

﴿Only those believe in Our signs﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿who, when they are reminded by them﴾ are admonished by them, ﴿fall down in prostration﴾ and ﴿glorify﴾ [God], ﴿with praise of their Lord﴾ i.e., they say: "Glory be to God and praise be to Him," ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾ towards faith and obedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 16:

﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾ rise up [i.e., are lifted] ﴿from the beds﴾ the places of lying down, with their bedding, for their prayer at night, in tahajjud (voluntary night prayer). ﴿They call upon their Lord in fear﴾ of His punishment ﴿and in hope﴾ of His mercy. ﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾ they give in charity.

﴿So no soul knows what has been hidden﴾ *khubi'a* (it was concealed). And in one recitation (*qira'a*, a transmitted mode of reciting the Qur'an), the *ya'* is vowelless (*sukun*), making the verb *mudari'* (present tense): *ukhfi*. ﴿Of comfort for the eyes﴾ is what their eyes are cooled by.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 18:

﴿Is he who is a believer like one who is defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.﴾ That is, the believers and the defiantly disobedient (are not equal).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 19:

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of refuge as a lodging (nuzulan)﴾ — it is what is prepared for the guest.
And as for those who defied (fasaqu): by disbelief and denial.

We will surely make them taste the nearer punishment (ʿadhāb al-adnā), (meaning) the punishment of this world: by killing, captivity, drought for years, and sicknesses, ﴿short of﴾ (i.e., before) ﴿the greater punishment﴾ (ʿadhāb al-akbar), the punishment of the Hereafter, ﴿so that perhaps they﴾ (i.e., those among them who remain) ﴿will return﴾ to faith.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 22:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿then turns away from them﴾ i.e., there is no one more unjust than him. ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾ the polytheists.

And We certainly gave Moses the Book (al-Kitab), meaning the Torah (al-Tawrah): ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾ ﴿So do not be in doubt (shakk) about meeting him﴾, and they had met on the night of the Night Journey (al-Isra'). ﴿And We made it﴾, meaning Moses or the Book, ﴿a guidance﴾, guiding.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 32, verse 24:**

﴿And We made among them leaders﴾ (*a'immah*), with *tahqiq al-hamzatayn* (pronouncing both hamzas clearly) and *ibdal al-thaniyah yā'* (changing the second hamza to a yā'): leaders, ﴿guiding﴾ the people ﴿by Our command when they were patient﴾ in their religion and patient in the trials from their enemy. In another reading, لِمَا is read with a kasra on the lām and a light mīm: ﴿and they were certain of Our signs﴾ that indicate Our power and Our oneness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 25:

﴿Indeed, your Lord – He will decide between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ regarding the matter of the religion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 26:

﴿Do they not see how many generations We destroyed before them,﴾ meaning: it becomes clear to the disbelievers of Makkah how much We destroyed ﴿of the generations﴾, the nations, because of their disbelief. ﴿Through whose dwellings they walk.﴾ "Walk" is a circumstantial state (hal) referring to the pronoun in "for them". ﴿In their dwellings﴾ means in their journeys to al-Sham and elsewhere, so that they may take heed. ﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾ meaning proofs of Our power. ﴿Do they not listen?﴾ meaning listening of reflection and admonition.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 27:

﴿Do they not see that We drive the water to the barren land⟩ the dry land in which there is no vegetation, ﴿so We bring forth thereby crops from which eat their cattle and themselves. Will they not see?⟩ this, so that they know that We are able to restore them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 28:

﴿And they say﴾ to the believers, ﴿"When is this victory" between us and you?﴾

﴿Say: "On the Day of Victory"﴾ by the sending down of punishment upon them, ﴿their faith will not benefit those who disbelieved, nor will they be reprieved﴾, meaning they will not be granted delay for repentance or for an excuse.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 32, verse 30:

﴿So turn away from them and wait﴾ for the descent of punishment upon them. ﴿Indeed, they are waiting﴾ for you, for an event to befall you, death or killing, so that they may be relieved of you. And this was before the command to fight them.
